errors.description: The contrast strip runs lengthwise down the cuff - from the sleeve-join seam straight down to the hem, perpendicular to the cuff's edges. The drawn strip runs the other way: it encircles the wrist, parallel to the cuff's two edges, centred at mid-height of the band.
errors.expected: a 1 cm contrast strip encircling the wrist, parallel to the cuff's two edges, centred at mid-height of the cuff band, with the cuff button sitting on the strip
errors.actual: a ~1 cm navy strip running across the band from the sleeve seam to the hem, the button sitting on it
errors.correction: Rotate the strip 90 degrees relative to the cuff: it must run around the wrist parallel to the cuff's hem and sleeve-join edges, not from one edge to the other.

errors.description: With the strip running the wrong way the option is not distinguishable from a generic contrast placket-style stripe, and the drawn relationship - a mid-band contrast band circling the cuff - is lost.
errors.expected: the exact drawn option: contrast strip through the centre of the cuff, encircling it
errors.actual: a vertical contrast stripe crossing the cuff band

lockedFeatures: strip width is close to the drawn 1 cm relative to the cuff band
cuff button sits ON the contrast strip, exactly the relationship drawn
strip is truly spliced in with a stitched seam along each long edge, not a ribbon laid on the surface
cuff otherwise entirely white, as drawn
no notation red (attempt 2 rendered this strip in the drawing's notation red); navy contrast used instead
no traced annotations: no '1cm' text, no arrow, no leader line
real photograph on a male model, clean seamless light-grey studio background, cuff dominant in frame
notes: Attempt 3 of 3 - UNMET, and a REGRESSION. ATTEMPT 2 (candidate-2.png) IS THE BETTER ARTIFACT AND A HUMAN SHOULD LOOK AT IT: in attempt 2 the strip correctly encircles the wrist parallel to the cuff edges at mid-band height with the button sitting on it, and the width reads close to the drawn 1 cm. Its defects are cosmetic - it was rendered in the drawing's notation red and as a satin ribbon rather than spliced cotton. Attempt 3 fixed the fabric and colour and rotated the strip the wrong way. Attempt 1 had the same wrong orientation as attempt 3. Reading of the drawing: it is a 3/4 view of an isolated cuff drum whose axis runs left-right in the image, so the drawn vertical strip runs AROUND the wrist. This is corroborated by the sibling upper/lower options, whose '1/2' division line is drawn in the same direction and must run around the wrist for 'upper portion'/'lower portion of sleeve cuff' to mean anything. Do not ship candidate-3.
